title: First-time dev here! Been working on my indie game "Bug Bound" for a month (using AI tools) — would love your feedback!
author: Other_Education_7923
selftext:
Hey everyone! 👋

As a first-time solo dev, I've spent the past month building an indie game called **Bug Bound**, and I just uploaded an early version of it to Itch.io!

Since I'm building this from scratch, I've been experimenting with using AI tools to help with different parts of the development process.

The game features:

* **Terrarium management & bug collecting**
* **Aphid nectar bar drink processing**
* Custom tilemaps and pixel art style
* A **payload train-defense horde survival mode**

Since I'm still learning the ropes, I would honestly love to hear what you guys think about the concept, the setup, or anything else. If you have a few minutes to check it out on Itch, any honest feedback, critiques, or advice on what I should focus on next would mean the world to me!

🔗 **Check it out here:** 

[https://dheerajsuresh.itch.io/bug-bound](https://dheerajsuresh.itch.io/bug-bound)

Let me know what you think in the comments! 👇

comments.author: WhosLive
comments.body: congrats on getting a first build out after a month. a lot of people find that for a first game the best feedback comes from watching someone play it cold, so a short screen recording of a new player is worth trying. with that many systems (terrarium, bar, train defense) it usually helps to polish one loop until it feels good before adding more. also worth noting in the page which parts were AI assisted, since players tend to respond better when that's upfront.
